earlier lawsuit accusing it of promoting “illegal gambling.”
New York Drags Polymarket to Court
The state alleged in its lawsuit that Polymarket’s prediction markets constitute gambling, as the outcomes on which users bet are “uncertain” and beyond their “control.”

The lawsuit filed in a state court in Manhattan mentioned that Polymarket has not obtained a license from the New York State Gaming Commission, allowing it to evade tax obligations similar to those of “licensed casinos” and “mobile sports gambling platforms.”
James asked the court to order Polymarket to forfeit all “illegal gains,” pay “restitution” to consumers who were harmed and pay fines equal to three times those profits.
“By skirting New York’s laws, Polymarket is targeting the most vulnerable and depriving New York families of critical services and support,” James said.

children: Polymarket’s Response
Polymarket filed a countersuit against James and state officials on Thursday evening, Reuters reported, arguing the CFTC has exclusive authority to regulate prediction markets.
Daniel Wallach
, a sports betting and gaming lawyer, also reported on X that Polymarket removed James’s civil enforcement action from state court to federal court in the Southern District of New York.
Polymarket didn’t immediately return Benzinga’s request for comment.
Update: Polymarket has removed the New York AG’s civil enforcement action to federal court in the SDNY
